formats.name: Bus shelter poster, 47.5 x 68.5 in (OAAA standard)

dpi.note: OAAA and TARC: 80-100 ppi at full size (160-200 at 1/2 scale); Pace: 150 dpi at full size, 300 at half size; TARC prefers 300 ppi at half scale (= 150 full).

file.notes: TARC: print-quality PDF, fonts outlined, crop marks and bleed; or packaged InDesign/Illustrator; or PSD with trim/safety marked. Half-scale mechanical (23.75 x 34.25 in) is the OAAA convention.

formats.material: Backlit: Duratrans, polypropylene, encapsulated 80 lb wet-strength paper, 0.020 styrene or opaline (Pace/Intersection). OAAA: reverse printing preferred for backlit; single section only.
formats.notes: OAAA cheat sheet and Pace (Intersection, Chicago) list 68.5 h x 47.5 w with live = finished; safety 65 x 44 (Pace, TARC). OAAA's bus shelter page gives copy area 67 x 46 (the area the frame shows) but an overall of 48 x 69 with H/W labels swapped relative to the copy area; treat 47.5 x 68.5 as trim. TARC says '68.5h x 47.5w with 1/4 in bleed on all four sides' and does not say whether 68.5 x 47.5 includes it; Pace lists no bleed. bleed_in=0 here; ask the operator. Dimensions vary by market and operator.

formats.name: Bus shelter poster, 47.25 x 68.25 in trim

file.notes: UWF: 'Set your document to this size with no bleed'; minimum 200 dpi at exact poster size, saved as PDF.

formats.material: Vancouver/Outfront: 7 pt coated translucent bristol, screen printed one side; no styrene faces; do not laminate (heat makes it brittle behind glass).
formats.notes: Trim 47-1/4 x 68-1/4, visible opening 45 x 66-1/4, full safety 42-1/2 x 64-11/16 (UWF; same figures in City of Vancouver's Outfront Media shelter guidelines, which could not be fetched directly: Cloudflare-blocked, figures from its indexed text). Color mode not stated (null). Safe inset computed from trim minus safety.

formats.placement: Street light-pole banner (pole pockets top and bottom)
formats.name: Pole banner, 18 x 36 in
formats.color: Full-color process; color mode not specified by sources

file.notes: Banners.com: vector (AI, EPS, PDF) ideal; outline fonts. Show Your Logo accepts ai, eps, pdf, jpg, png, psd, tif (50 MB max). Double-sided = two art files.

formats.material: 13 oz vinyl standard; 18 oz blockout/opaque scrim vinyl for year-round or double-sided (Banners.com; Show Your Logo uses Titan 18 oz opaque scrim).
formats.notes: Pole pockets consume the top and bottom 3-4 in of the face (Banners.com); Show Your Logo uses 3 in pockets top/bottom (poles up to 1.25 in dia) and its full-color safe area is listed 'plus bleed' without a bleed amount, so bleed_in=null; canvas = trim at 150 dpi with no bleed. Keep critical content 1 in+ inside all edges (Banners.com). Seattle's approved art example shows a 30 x 60 finished banner with 4 in bleed top & bottom into welded 3 in pockets; pocket/hem allowance is printer-specific, get the printer's template.

formats.color: CMYK typical; not stated by OAAA

file.notes: Not stated; get the airport media owner's template.

formats.material: Backlit. Screen print or litho on 0.010 clear cellulose or vinyl (print two sides if litho), or photographic Varicolor/Duratrans (OAAA).

formats.name: T-shirt front, large 15 x 18 in

dpi.note: Printful: at least 150 DPI, best not to exceed 300.

formats.color: sRGB (sRGB IEC61966-2.1); printer converts to CMYK. No Pantone matching on DTG.

file.notes: PNG with transparent background preferred.

formats.notes: Printful 3001 file guidelines: Front, from size L: 15 x 18 in. Printful's 15 x 18 'large_front' replaced the legacy 12 x 16 front on 3001 (L-5XL), 3413 (L-4XL) and Cotton Heritage MC1082 (M-3XL). Placement (secondary, Printify): front print about 2-3 in below the neckline (3 in for a 6-8 in logo); back about 4-6 in below the collar; left chest 2.5-5 in square, 4-6 in below the collar. Printful: avoid semi-transparency (halftone instead); leave black areas transparent on black garments; no white ink on white garments; avoid perfect borders. Screen-print maxima from Custom Ink were not found (Custom Ink pages not indexed); 12 x 16 in is the widely cited industry max.
